card: Relaxes the repository's clang-format configuration to permit single-line loops and inline template declarations. The previous strict rules conflict with existing developer habits, causing unwanted diff churn during local formatting runs and adding friction to PR reviews. Grep counts cited by the author show over 100 single-line loops and over 160 inline template declarations already present across the src/ tree.
evidence: PR description demonstrates existing codebase patterns via grep: 111 single-line for-loops in src/ ('git grep --line-number --perl-regexp "^\s*for \([^)]+\) [^{]+;$" ./src/') and 162 inline template declarations ('git grep --line-number --perl-regexp "^\s*template\s*<.*>\s*(?:class|struct|[A-Za-z_])"').
problem: The previous clang-format configuration enforces line breaks on short loops and template declarations, conflicting with common practices across the codebase. Developers running clang-format locally experience unwanted diff churn, and reviewers face friction pointing out formatting mismatches that are widely ignored.

risk.why: A mistake in clang-format settings would only cause unintended code reformatting during local or automated styling passes.

summary: Updates src/.clang-format to set AllowShortLoopsOnASingleLine to true and AlwaysBreakTemplateDeclarations to No. This relaxes code formatting rules to permit single-line loops and inline template declarations.
